D.why: The most gown-like shape: an ash A-line skirt with a pale front panel, a violet hem, waist and crown gems, and a tall fan crown, all in the right palette.
D.fix: Slim the shoulder-width grey block sleeves and lean the skirt panels further out so the hem clearly outflares the elbows.

E.why: The most distinctive family: a bone-spike crown and bone-and-charcoal rib pleats with violet seams that suit the giants'-bones zone and read from above.
E.fix: Close the split pleats into one continuous bell that carries round the back, and narrow the boxy sleeves.

C.why: The best true bell from the hip, with charred petals and a violet hem, ruined by huge black block sleeves and an overall darkness that vanishes at night.
C.fix: Slim the black sleeves and add an ash or bone layer to the bodice and underskirt so the gown has a light value from above.

B.why: The violet halo is a good place for light, but the all-grey boxy torso and shoulder-width sleeves read as armour, and the stepped skirt is short and stiff.
B.fix: Slim and darken the sleeves, lengthen and widen the bell, and swap the gold waist trim for bone or violet.

F.why: The pale ash tiered skirt flares well, but the hood and spike headpiece and the dominant dark block sleeves read as a monk, not a lady.
F.fix: Open the hood into a crown or halo, slim the sleeves, and char the lowest skirt tier with a violet edge.

A.why: Black block sleeves wider than the shoulders and a hip shelf make a square armoured outline, and the skirt barely widens.
A.fix: Cut the sleeves slim, remove the hip shelf, and build a real flared skirt from the hip with a bone crown and violet seams.

notes: No candidate solved slim sleeves: every set still wears block sleeves the width of the shoulders, and that remains the top fix across the run. D and E are close. D is the prettiest gown shape and E is the most inventive family. A builder who merged C's bell, E's crown and pleats and D's palette with slim sleeves would win.
